# Freeze store integrity maintenance

Ensure the `TextFileBasedViolationStore` maintains the integrity of its `stored.rules` index and files.

Setting `default.integrity` to `repair` will check the index and folder as they are on disk during initialization, even if the same folder was initialized before. Defaulting to `ignore` which checks nothing.

If an entry points to a path that is not a regular file directly within the folder, it is broken. This also applies if the file name is not a valid path.

If an entry is not broken and its file has no violations it is resolved. Files that only contain line breaks are also resolved.

Entries that point to the same file name are shared, even if nothing exists with that name. If multiple entries point to the same file they are also shared. Including through a symbolic or hard link. Even if that file is outside the folder.

The `TextFileBasedViolationStore` will not touch any shared entries or files that no entry points to. If an entry is shared and anything else it will remain shared.

When set to `repair` broken entries will be discarded.

When set to `repair` resolved entries and the file they point to will be discarded. If a resolved entry is a symbolic link the file it points to will be deleted as well.

If using `repair` and saving no violations for a known rule it will forget the rule. Its entry will be removed and its file as well. Unless another entry is sharing that file. In which case only the entry will be removed. Even if it points outside the folder. If using `repair` and saving no violations for an unknown rule nothing will be saved.

If it cannot delete the file of a rule it is forgetting it will fail to save and leave the entry.

The [`TextFileBasedViolationStore`](file:///app/archunit/src/main/java/com/tngtech/archunit/library/freeze/TextFileBasedViolationStore.java#L65) has been enhanced to support integrity maintenance for its `stored.rules` index and files according to the specification.

### Summary of Changes

1. **Configuration Property**:
   - Added configuration property `default.integrity` (defaulting to `"ignore"`).
   - When set to `"repair"`, the store checks the index and directory contents as they are on disk during initialization via [`repairIntegrity`](file:///app/archunit/src/main/java/com/tngtech/archunit/library/freeze/TextFileBasedViolationStore.java#L210), reloading properties from disk even if the folder was initialized previously.
   - When set to `"ignore"` (or omitted), nothing is checked.

2. **Integrity Verification & Classification**:
   - **Broken Entries**: An entry is marked broken if its target is not a regular file directly within the store folder (including non-existent files, directories, paths with subdirectories or parent directories, absolute paths, broken symlinks, symlinks to directories, or invalid paths). Broken unshared entries are discarded from `stored.rules`.
   - **Resolved Entries**: An entry is resolved if it is not broken and its violation file contains no violations (empty or only line breaks: `\n`, `\r\n`, or `\r`). Resolved unshared entries are removed from `stored.rules`, and their files are deleted. If a resolved entry is a symbolic link, both the symbolic link and the file it points to are deleted.
   - **Shared Entries**: Entries pointing to the same file name (even if the file does not exist) or pointing to the same file on disk (including through symbolic links or hard links, even outside the store folder) are marked as shared. Shared entries and files that no entry points to are never modified or deleted during repair.

3. **Rule Forgetting on Save**:
   - In [`save(ArchRule, List<String>)`](file:///app/archunit/src/main/java/com/tngtech/archunit/library/freeze/TextFileBasedViolationStore.java#L164), when `default.integrity` is `repair` and saving no violations (`violations.isEmpty()`):
     - If the rule is unknown: nothing is saved or created.
     - If the rule is known: the rule is forgotten. Its entry is removed from `stored.rules` and its file is deleted (even if pointing outside the store folder). If another entry shares that file, only the entry is removed while the file is preserved.
     - If the file cannot be deleted, saving fails with a [`StoreUpdateFailedException`](file:///app/archunit/src/main/java/com/tngtech/archunit/library/freeze/StoreUpdateFailedException.java) and the rule's entry is left in `stored.rules`.

4. **Synchronized State**:
   - Enhanced [`FileSyncedProperties`](file:///app/archunit/src/main/java/com/tngtech/archunit/library/freeze/TextFileBasedViolationStore.java#L479) with `reload()`, `getEntries()`, `remove(String)`, and `removeAll(Collection<String>)` methods with synchronization for thread safety.

### Verification

All existing and newly added test suites were executed and verified:
- Created [`TextFileBasedViolationStoreIntegrityTest`](file:///app/archunit/src/test/java/com/tngtech/archunit/library/freeze/TextFileBasedViolationStoreIntegrityTest.java) with 15 test cases covering:
  - Default integrity behavior (`ignore`).
  - Discarding broken entries (non-existent, subfolder, parent, directory, broken symlink, symlink to directory, invalid paths).
  - Discarding resolved entries (empty files, line breaks `\n`, `\r\n`, `\r`, symlinks, symlink chains) while preserving files with violations.
  - Preserving shared entries (same file name when non-existent, symlinks, hardlinks, outside folder).
  - Preserving orphan files unreferenced by any entry.
  - Checking disk state even if the folder was initialized before.
  - Forgetting known rules on empty violations, including shared-file preservation and files outside the folder.
  - Ignoring unknown rules when saving empty violations without updating the store.
  - Retaining entries and failing when file deletion cannot be performed.
- Executed `./gradlew :archunit:test` across the entire ArchUnit test suite, with all tests passing successfully.
